ECE 6390 / Spacecraft systems

Heat & radiator

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how transmitter efficiency sets the waste heat that a radiator must reject.

An amplifier delivering RF power PRF at efficiency ηPA draws PRF/ηPA of DC power. Its waste heat is PRF(1/ηPA − 1), before other spacecraft heat loads are added.

A lumped radiating surface satisfies Q = εσA(T⁴ − Tenv⁴) at steady state. Temperature is in kelvin, area in m², and σ ≈ 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/(m² K⁴).

Increasing radiator area or emissivity supports the same heat flow at a lower temperature. This model assumes uniform temperatures and a specified effective environment; real surfaces also depend on illumination and view factors.

Example

A 100 W RF output at 50% efficiency draws 200 W and produces 100 W of amplifier heat. At 25% efficiency, the same RF output produces 300 W of heat.
